question: What are the differences between encoder-decoder and causal/non-causal decoder-only LMs?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: Answer frames the comparison as three Transformer-based LM architectures — encoder-decoder (ED), causal decoder-only (CD), and non-causal decoder-only (ND) — with self-attention as the core building block.
examples: All three are variants of the Transformer architecture built on self-attention
The comparison covers ED and two decoder-only variants, all Transformer-based

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: Answer defines CD models as a single Transformer stack trained to autoregressively predict a text sequence (next-token prediction), e.g., GPT.
examples: Decoder-only models with causal masking, predicting the next token autoregressively
GPT-series models: a single stack doing full language modeling

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: Answer describes ED models as having two stacks: a bidirectional encoder where each input token sees all others, and an autoregressive decoder with causal masking that conditions on encoder output via cross-attention in each block.
examples: Encoder uses bidirectional conditioning; decoder attends to encoder outputs via cross-attention
Two stacks: full self-attention over input, causal decoding with cross-attention layers

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: Answer explains that ND models (prefix LMs) use only a decoder but with a modified attention mask so a portion of the sequence is non-causal, bridging decoder-only and encoder-decoder architectures.
examples: Prefix LM: non-causal attention over the prefix, causal over the rest
ND modifies the attention mask to bridge CD and ED

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: Answer identifies at least one example of a pretrained encoder-decoder LM, such as BART or T5.
examples: BART and T5 use encoder-decoder architectures
T5 follows the originally proposed encoder-decoder form

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: Answer notes that most recent LLMs are causal decoder-only models, while non-causal decoders (e.g., Liu et al. 2018; Dong et al. 2019) have seen limited adoption.
examples: Despite the bridge design, ND architectures are rarely used

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: Answer cites that encoder-decoder models outperform decoder-only LMs for transfer learning, i.e., fine-tuning a pretrained model on a single downstream task (Raffel et al.).
examples: ED models outperform decoder-only for transfer learning
ED wins when fine-tuning on a single downstream task

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: Answer reports the mixed zero-shot comparison: CD models with full language modeling achieve best zero-shot generalization right after pretraining, while ED models with masked language modeling achieve best zero-shot after multitask finetuning.
examples: CD best zero-shot right after pretraining; ED with MLM best after multitask finetuning
Comparisons are mixed depending on pretraining objective and finetuning setup
